dedupe_keys.name: usace disaster impact models hurricane debris commodities temporary roofing and housing estimates

description: The US Army Corps of Engineers runs a set of disaster impact models that use geospatial tools to estimate, ahead of a hurricane, the likely debris volumes, needs for water and ice commodities, the number of people and households within hurricane-force winds, and the need for temporary roofing and temporary housing. The page read on 2026-09-28 explains that estimates start about three days before a forecast landfall, that their release depends on National Hurricane Center and Central Pacific Hurricane Center forecast times and storm speed, that the models apply to the US East and Gulf Coasts, the Caribbean islands and the Pacific islands, and that mission models for debris, commodities, roofing and housing follow about two days before landfall; results are posted on the page for storms of interest. Coverage is US hurricane-exposed regions. Access to posted results is free; the model code is not published and no licence is stated. Caveats: the page itself warns the estimates are general because of forecast uncertainty and are meant to set the scale and scope of an event. It supports emergency response and debris management planning for hurricanes, including exposure of buildings and waste systems. No related USACE emergency model record is catalogued; FEMA Hazus complements it.
